title: Unit – 5 : Session – 9 : SLO – 1  |  Instruction Formats (Zero/One/Two/Three-Address)
sections: I. Multiple Choice
1. C) Stack — zero-address instructions operate on the stack.
2. D) Accumulator — the one-address format uses the accumulator as the implicit operand.
3. B) Destination operand — in the two-address format the result overwrites the destination.
II. Fill in the Blanks
1. postfix — zero-address format is ideal for postfix (reverse-Polish) expressions.
2. accumulator — one-address format uses the accumulator for intermediate calculations.
3. three — the three-address format explicitly specifies three operands (two sources + destination).
III. True or False
1. FALSE — zero-address instructions take operands implicitly from the stack.
2. TRUE.
3. TRUE — an explicit destination removes the need for temporary memory.
IV. Match the Following
A) Zero Address — 1) Stack-based.
B) One Address — 2) Accumulator.
C) Two Address — 3) Destination overwritten.
D) Three Address — 4) Three explicit operands.
V. Numerical Answers
1. Zero-address code for (A + B) * (C + D):  PUSH A; PUSH B; ADD; PUSH C; PUSH D; ADD; MUL — the stack machine leaves (A+B)*(C+D) on top.
2. 4 bits — log2(16) = 4 bits encode 16 registers.
3. 24 bits — 8-bit opcode + 16-bit address = 24 bits per instruction.
